title: Larry, Chief Mouser to the Cabinet Office
hook: A rescue tabby from Battersea has outlasted a string of prime ministers.
peek: Larry is the cat who lives at 10 Downing Street. He arrived from a London rescue centre in 2011, and because he belongs to the staff rather than the prime minister, he stays while governments come and go.
lede: In February 2011, a brown and white tabby from Battersea Dogs and Cats Home moved into 10 Downing Street. Larry was given the title Chief Mouser to the Cabinet Office, the first cat to hold it officially. He belongs to the civil service staff rather than to any prime minister, so when leaders move out, Larry stays.

bullets.text: Larry arrived under David Cameron and was still in post through Theresa May, Boris Johnson, Liz Truss, Rishi Sunak and, by 2024, Keir Starmer. He has become a fixture of news footage outside the famous black door.
The London rescue centre, founded in the 1860s, has supplied several government cats. Its rehoming of Larry made it one of the best-known adoptions in Britain.
From 2016 the Foreign Office had its own Battersea cat, Palmerston. Newspapers covered their standoffs on Downing Street with mock seriousness until Palmerston retired in 2020.
Before Larry, a black and white stray named Humphrey served from 1989 to 1997, under Margaret Thatcher, John Major and Tony Blair. Cats have lived at Downing Street on and off for about a century.
Larry is said to be wary of strangers, which is typical of cats. Most purr and relax around a few trusted people rather than a crowd of photographers.
Photographers have caught him in plenty of half-closed-eye moments on the doorstep. To another cat, that slow blink is a friendly signal, a polite way of saying I mean no harm.
